summary: Implemented async click ingestion queue with Celery/Redis, background worker with atomic idempotency (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), owner-scoped analytics API with date filters, SHA-256 IP hashing, 30-day retention purge, and graceful queue outage fallback.
evidence: 50/50 automated unit, security, caching, queue, idempotency, and retention tests passing in pytest (apps/api/tests/test_analytics_and_jobs.py).
Live probe verified: two redirects enqueued click tasks processed by Celery worker into PostgreSQL, updating GET /links/{id}/analytics click count.
Idempotency verified: replaying identical event_id payload produces duplicate_skipped with 1 row in click_events.
Privacy verified: IP addresses stored strictly as 64-char SHA-256 hashes, raw IPs never stored.
Retention purge verified: POST /links/maintenance/purge-clicks purged records older than 30-day cutoff.
Queue outage drill verified: redirect path returns HTTP 302 cleanly when Celery/Redis is down.
